Bhagavad Gita, Chapter 3, Verse 20

“Indeed, it was by action alone that Janaka and others attained perfection. You should act with a view to the welfare of the world as well.”

Krishna cites a precedent Arjuna knows — Janaka, a king who ruled and was still free. And a second motive arrives here: loka-sangraha, the holding together of the world.
